question: What is the minimum number of players a team must have for a match to start or continue?
expected_answer: Seven. A match may not start or continue if either team has fewer than seven players.

question: How long does a match last?
expected_answer: Two equal halves of 45 minutes; this may be reduced only by agreement between the referee and both teams before the start and in accordance with competition rules.

What items make up a player's compulsory equipment?

question: Who chaired the 140th Annual General Meeting of The IFAB, and where was it held?
expected_answer: Mike Jones, President of The Football Association of Wales, chaired it. It took place in Hensol, Wales, on 28 February 2026.

question: For how long may a goalkeeper control the ball with their hands before a corner kick is awarded?
expected_answer: More than eight seconds; the referee visually counts down the last five seconds.

question: When is a player in an offside position?
expected_answer: When any part of the head, body or feet is in the opponents' half (excluding the halfway line) and nearer to the opponents' goal line than both the ball and the second-last opponent. Hands and arms are not considered. Being level with the second-last opponent or the last two opponents is not offside.

question: When is touching the ball with the hand or arm a handball offence?
expected_answer: It is an offence if the player deliberately touches the ball with the hand/arm, or touches it when the hand/arm has made the body unnaturally bigger (position not a consequence of or justifiable by the body movement). Also if they score directly from the hand/arm or immediately after the ball touched it, even if accidental. Not every touch is an offence.

question: What happens if the ball touches the referee and goes directly into the goal?
expected_answer: The ball is out of play and play is restarted with a dropped ball; no goal is awarded.

question: What must a substituted player do under the time-limited substitution rule, and what happens if they take too long?
expected_answer: They must leave the field within ten seconds of the substitution board or signal. If they do not, they must still leave but the substitute may not enter until the first stoppage after one minute (running clock) following the restart.

question: What happens when a team deliberately delays a throw-in?
expected_answer: The referee whistles, signals and starts a visual five-second countdown. If the ball is not in play at the end, the throw-in is awarded to the opposing team at the same position.

question: In which situations does an injured player not have to leave the field of play after assessment or treatment?
expected_answer: Goalkeeper injured; goalkeeper and outfield player collided; players of the same team collided; severe injury (e.g. head injury, cardiac issue, life-threatening event); injury from a physical offence for which the opponent is cautioned or sent off; a penalty kick has been awarded and the injured player is the kicker. Also if the player indicates no medical attention is needed (unless play was stopped for the injury) or leaves voluntarily without delaying the restart.
notes: Held out. The first six items are the Law 5 list; the last two come from the Circular 34 / protocol wording.

question: What does the goalkeeper-injury trial require, and are there exceptions?
expected_answer: When the goalkeeper has an actual or suspected injury that stops play, is assessed or treated on the field, or the referee signals medical staff, an outfield player must leave for one minute after the restart (running clock). Exceptions include: goalkeeper says no treatment is needed (unless play was stopped for the injury), goalkeeper/outfield collision, severe injury, bleeding, injury from a physical offence for which a free kick is awarded and immediate treatment is needed. It is a trial protocol, not part of the Laws.

question: What additional kind of incident can the VAR review under the attacking set-piece trial?
expected_answer: An attacking-team offence before the ball is in play at an attacking free kick or corner kick, when it directly leads to a goal, a penalty kick, or a defending-team red-card offence (DOGSO, second yellow for DOGSO/SPA). It is a trial, not part of the Laws.

question: What is the sanction for a player who covers their mouth when communicating with an opponent?
expected_answer: If the competition has adopted the optional Law change from Circular 33, covering the mouth in a provocative, derisory or inflammatory manner is a sending-off offence. It is a competition option.
notes: Must carry the 'competition option' qualifier in the first sentence.

question: Can a player be sent off for what they say?
expected_answer: Yes. Using offensive, insulting or abusive language and/or action(s) is a sending-off offence. Dissent by word or action is a caution offence, and dissent or offensive language is also an indirect free kick offence.
notes: Known retrieval risk: the sending-off bullet sits in a different chunk from the caution list.

question: What is the penalty for a player who dives to win a free kick?
expected_answer: A caution (yellow card) for unsporting behaviour: attempting to deceive the referee, e.g. by feigning injury or pretending to have been fouled (simulation).
notes: Known retrieval miss: the question says 'dives', the Laws say 'simulation'.

question: Why is a goalkeeper allowed to hold the ball for six seconds?
expected_answer: The premise is wrong: the limit is eight seconds, after which a corner kick is awarded. A good answer corrects the premise. A plain refusal earns partial credit at most.
notes: Scored on whether the answer corrects the premise.

question: How many substitutes may be used in a friendly between senior 'A' international teams?
expected_answer: A maximum of eight may be used (up to fifteen may be named); both teams may agree to more, up to eleven, informing the referee before the match. Must not say six.
notes: Strikethrough test: the Law-changes section (p.170-171) shows struck-through 'six' beside 'eight'.

question: If the ball touches the referee inside the penalty area and goes into the goal, how is play restarted?
expected_answer: The ball is out of play and play restarts with a dropped ball. Because it was inside the penalty area, the ball is dropped for the defending team's goalkeeper; where a match official was hit, it is dropped at the position of the contact.

question: Which player has to leave the field under the goalkeeper-injury trial?
expected_answer: Under Protocol A the team captain leaves (unless the goalkeeper is the captain or the captain is the penalty kicker). Under Protocol B the coach nominates a player within ten seconds, and if none is nominated the captain leaves. It is a trial.
notes: Exceptions (goalkeeper is the captain; captain is the penalty kicker) are part of a complete answer.
